findings.title: SQL injection in data migration
findings.body: The migration string-interpolates the per-line host value directly into an INSERT statement: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)`. The `h` strings come from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which an admin controls. The model-level `validates_format_of :host` does NOT run during this raw INSERT, so values like `'); DROP TABLE users; --` would be inserted verbatim and could corrupt or destroy the database. Use parameterized SQL (e.g. `execute("INSERT ... VALUES (?, ?, ...)", h, category_id)`) or instantiate `EmbeddableHost.new(host: h, category_id: category_id).save(validate: false)` so input is escaped.

findings.title: Migration raises NoMethodError when embed_category was never set

The code then does `...[0]['id'].to_i`, which throws `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the migration, leaving the DB in a half-migrated state. Guard the lookup (e.g. check `result.cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing) and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when the join yields nothing.

findings.title: Admin embedding page cannot render existing embeddable_hosts
findings.body: `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids`, which only emits `embeddable_host_ids: [..]` on the parent and does NOT include the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the payload root. On the client, `store._hydrateEmbedded` then looks up each ID via `_lookupSubType('embeddable_host', ...)` which depends on `root['embeddable_hosts']` existing, finds nothing, and assigns `embedding.embeddable_hosts = [undefined, undefined, undefined]`. The Handlebars `{{#each embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` iterates those undefined entries and crashes the component when it dereferences `host.isNew` / `host.host`. As a result the page can't display any pre-existing hosts. Either include the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the response root (e.g. embed: :objects, or have the route do a separate `findAll('embeddable-host')`), or have the serializer/hydration fall back to a freshly-fetched list.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is blank
findings.body: `before_validation` unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`. If the attribute is nil or was never assigned (e.g. a Fabricator without a `host:`, or a controller call that omits the param), `sub!` is invoked on nil and raises `NoMethodError`, instead of being reported as a 422 validation error. Add `validates_presence_of :host`, guard the `sub!` (e.g. `self.host = (self.host || '').sub(...)` then assign back), and the model-level presence validation will then return clean errors.

Multiple admins can create duplicate rows for the same site, leaving stale rows that survive deletion and confuse the host picker. Add `validates :host, presence: true, uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }` on the model and `add_index :embeddable_hosts, :host, unique: true` (case-insensitive) in the migration so race conditions can't create duplicates.

Any existing entries containing `http://`, a trailing path, or characters outside `[a-z0-9\-\.]` are reproduced verbatim, then fail format validation when an admin later edits them. findings.title: Embedded topic silently created with wrong/nil category when host lookup fails
findings.body: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` returns false (not nil) when no host matches, and `try(:category_id)` then yields `nil`. The PostCreator is called with `category: nil`, which combined with `SiteSetting.allow_uncategorized_topics = false` and the Topic validates produce behaviour that diverges from the previous behaviour (`SiteSetting.embed_category`, which was always set or nil). Previously it was obvious when there was no configured category; now import can succeed silently or fail in `changed_to_category`, with no error surfaced to the caller. Consider raising or returning nil explicitly when `eh` is false so the caller knows the URL didn't match a configured host and the topic was not created in the expected category.
